claims.text: Labs: CBC, platelets, uric acid, liver tests, BUN and creatinine; urine protein by dipstick or urinalysis, and a 24-hour urine if delivery isn't urgent.
claims.quote: Laboratory tests include complete blood count (CBC), platelet count, uric acid, liver tests, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine, and, if creatinine is abnormal, creatinine clearance. Urine protein is checked with a dipstick or urinalysis; a 24-hour urine collection is begun, if urgent delivery is not indicated.

claims.text: Fetus: nonstress test or biophysical profile, plus estimated fetal weight.
claims.quote: The fetus is assessed using a nonstress test or biophysical profile (including assessment of amniotic fluid volume) and measurements to estimate fetal weight.

claims.text: Proteinuria is > 300 mg/24 hours or a protein/creatinine ratio ≥ 0.3; a negative dipstick doesn't rule out preeclampsia.
claims.quote: Proteinuria is defined as > 300 mg/24 hours. Alternatively, proteinuria is diagnosed based on a protein/creatinine ratio ≥ 0.3 or a dipstick reading of 2+; the dipstick test is used only if other quantitative methods are not available. Absence of proteinuria on less accurate tests (eg, urine dipstick testing, routine urinalysis) does not rule out preeclampsia.

claims.text: HELLP: LDH ≥ 600 IU/L, aminotransferases > 2 times normal and low platelets.
claims.quote: HELLP syndrome is classified as a severe form of preeclampsia and is diagnosed when all of the following are present: lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) ≥ 600 IU/L; aminotransferases > 2 times normal; and platelets

claims.text: New severe hypertension (no multifetal pregnancy or molar disease): consider tests for secondary causes such as renal artery stenosis, coarctation, Cushing syndrome, lupus and pheochromocytoma.
claims.quote: If severe hypertension occurs for the first time in pregnant women who do not have a multifetal pregnancy or gestational trophoblastic disease, tests to rule out other causes of hypertension (eg, renal artery stenosis, coarctation of the aorta, Cushing syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, pheochromocytoma) should be considered.
